1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; RDS: Relational Database Service; KMS: Key Management Service; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; ISO: International Organization for Standardization; SOC: System and Organization Controls; PCI: Payment Card Industry; SSL: Secure Sockets Layer; TLS: Transport Layer Security; SSE: server-side encryption; DSSE: dual-layer server-side encryption; CSPM: Cloud Security Posture Management

  • Explain the shared responsibility model: security of the cloud and security in the cloud
  • Say how responsibility shifts between Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS and AWS Lambda
  • Find compliance reports and agreements with AWS Artifact
  • Describe encryption in transit and at rest, AWS KMS and AWS Certificate Manager
  • Tell CloudTrail, CloudWatch, AWS Config and Control Tower apart, and know where logs live

2The shared responsibility model

Running case

Tidewater Asks Who Secures What

  • Tidewater's founder asks: "If we run on AWS, isn't AWS responsible for our security?"
  • The shop will use virtual servers, a managed database and serverless functions
  • An auditor wants proof of AWS's own compliance reports
  • The team wants to know who changed a setting, and whether resources follow its rules
  • Your job: draw the line between AWS's duties and Tidewater's, and pick the governance tools

Security of the Cloud, Security in the Cloud

  • Security is a shared responsibility between AWS and the customer
  • Security of the cloud: AWS protects the infrastructure that runs all AWS services
  • Security in the cloud: the customer's part, which depends on the services the customer chooses
  • Customers are also responsible for the sensitivity of their data and the laws that apply to them

Exam tip

"Of the cloud" is AWS; "in the cloud" is you.

What AWS Is Responsible For

  • AWS protects the hardware, software, networking and facilities that run its services
  • That runs from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to the physical security of the data centers
  • AWS provides services you can use securely, and independent auditors test its controls
  • AWS patches its own infrastructure and trains its own employees
Exam tip

Data center security, hardware and the virtualization layer are always AWS's responsibility.

What You Are Responsible For

  • It typically includes the guest operating system and its patches, installed applications and the security group firewall
  • Your data: how it is managed, classified and encrypted
  • Identity and access: who can do what, set with IAM (Module 4)
  • The more abstracted the service, the less you configure, but your data and access stay yours
  • Your duties are set by the services you select
Exam tip

Data, access and the configuration of what you deploy are always yours.

Inherited, Shared and Customer-Specific Controls

  • Inherited controls: you fully inherit them from AWS, such as physical and environmental controls
  • Shared controls: both sides apply them in their own context: patch management, configuration management, awareness and training
  • Customer-specific controls: yours alone, set by your application, such as routing data within security zones

Exam tip

Shared controls to remember: patching, configuration and training.

Responsibility Shifts With the Service

  • Amazon EC2: you manage the guest operating system, software and security groups
  • Amazon RDS: AWS also manages OS and database patching, backups and failover
  • AWS Lambda: AWS manages servers, patching, capacity and scaling
  • A managed service moves work to AWS, never your data and access duties

Exam tip

From EC2 to RDS to Lambda, AWS takes on more of the stack.

Amazon EC2: Most of the Management Is Yours

  • Amazon EC2 is infrastructure as a service: the customer handles nearly all security configuration and management of the instance
  • You apply guest operating system updates and security patches
  • You manage the software and utilities you install, and the security group firewall
  • AWS manages the hardware layers, so you do not run server hardware
  • Updating an OS or database by hand can cause user errors and downtime
Exam tip

Patching the operating system of an EC2 instance is your job, not AWS's.

Amazon RDS: AWS Runs the Database Platform

Task On premises Amazon EC2 Amazon RDS
Application optimization You You You
Database software and OS patching You You AWS
Backups, scaling, high availability You You AWS
Server maintenance, hardware, power You AWS AWS
  • You still tune queries and control access with IAM and VPC security groups
Exam tip

On RDS, AWS patches the engine and the OS; you tune the queries and control access.

AWS Lambda and Other Abstracted Services

  • AWS Lambda runs your code without you provisioning or managing servers
  • AWS manages server maintenance, capacity, scaling and patching; you provide the code, its permissions and your data
  • Amazon S3 and DynamoDB: AWS operates the infrastructure, operating system and platform
  • You use endpoints to store data, and manage your data, encryption options, classification and IAM permissions
  • Your duties also follow your data and the laws that apply to it
Exam tip

On abstracted services you give up servers, not responsibility for data and access.

Who Is Responsible?

Task Who
Physical security of the data center AWS
The hypervisor and host operating system AWS
Patching the guest OS on an EC2 instance Customer
Patching the database engine on Amazon RDS AWS
Setting a security group rule Customer
Deciding who may read an S3 bucket Customer
Exam tip

Ask two questions: is it infrastructure AWS runs, and which service is it on?

Common Traps: Shared Responsibility

  • "AWS is responsible for my data" is wrong: you classify, protect and control access to your data
  • "A managed service means no security work" is wrong: access, data and settings remain yours
  • Patching is shared, not one-sided: AWS patches its infrastructure, you patch what you run
  • Responsibility is not fixed: it shifts with the service
  • Compliance is shared too: AWS has certifications, you follow your laws
Exam tip

A statement that says AWS handles everything, or that you handle everything, is usually wrong.

3Compliance, encryption, logging and governance

AWS Compliance Programs and Your Part

  • AWS compliance programs help customers understand the controls in place at AWS
  • Three groups: certifications and attestations, laws, regulations and privacy, and alignments and frameworks
  • Examples: ISO 27001, SOC 1, 2 and 3, PCI DSS (global), HIPAA (US) and GDPR (Europe)
  • Independent auditors assess many of them
  • You remain responsible for complying with the laws and rules that apply to your business
Exam tip

AWS's certifications cover AWS's side; your compliance is still your job.

AWS Artifact: Reports and Agreements

  • AWS Artifact gives on-demand downloads of AWS security and compliance documents
  • Reports: for example ISO, PCI and SOC reports and certifications from accreditation bodies
  • Agreements: review, accept and track your agreements with AWS, for one account or many accounts in an organization
  • Give the documents to auditors or regulators as audit artifacts
  • Documents and agreements are free of charge; you still produce your own evidence

Exam tip

Where do I find AWS's compliance reports? AWS Artifact.

Compliance Varies by Location, Industry and Service

  • Needs differ by country and industry: HIPAA for US health data, GDPR for personal data in Europe, PCI DSS for payment cards
  • AWS publishes AWS Services in Scope by Compliance Program: not every service is in scope for every program
  • Generally available features are considered in scope unless excluded; a service missing from a list is not forbidden
  • You decide how a service affects your compliance, based on your data
  • Check the list for both the program and the service
Exam tip

Before relying on a service for regulated data, check it is in scope for the program you need.

Encryption: In Transit and At Rest [Verify live]

  • In transit: data is protected as it travels, using SSL/TLS
  • At rest: stored data is encrypted by the service (server-side) or by you before upload (client-side)
  • Amazon S3 encrypts every new object at rest by default with SSE-S3, since 5 January 2023; you can choose SSE-KMS, DSSE-KMS or SSE-C
  • With client-side encryption you manage the process and the keys
  • As of 4 November 2026: check the S3 documentation for current defaults

Exam tip

Moving across a network: in transit. Sitting on a disk or in a bucket: at rest.

AWS KMS and AWS Certificate Manager

  • AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) creates and controls the keys that encrypt and sign your data
  • KMS keys are protected by hardware security modules and never leave KMS unencrypted; key policies control who may use them
  • AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) creates, stores and renews SSL/TLS certificates for AWS websites and applications
  • Certificates managed with ACM have no additional charge; you pay for the resources you run
  • KMS serves encryption at rest; ACM serves encryption in transit
Exam tip

Encryption keys: KMS. TLS certificates: ACM.

Where to Find Logs

  • AWS CloudTrail records account activity, meaning API (application programming interface) calls: who did what, and when; trails deliver events to an Amazon S3 bucket
  • Amazon CloudWatch Logs collects logs from AWS services and your applications
  • VPC Flow Logs capture IP traffic to and from network interfaces and publish to CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 or Amazon Data Firehose

Exam tip

API activity: CloudTrail. Network traffic: VPC Flow Logs. Service and application logs: CloudWatch Logs.

AWS CloudTrail: Who Did What, and When

  • AWS CloudTrail supports auditing, governance and compliance by recording actions of a user, role or AWS service as events
  • It records actions from the console, the command line interface (CLI), software development kits (SDKs) and APIs
  • Event history is a viewable, searchable record of the past 90 days of management events in a Region, with no CloudTrail charge to view
  • Trails and CloudTrail Lake keep events for longer
  • It shows who acted, on what and when
Exam tip

Who deleted that resource, and when? CloudTrail.

Amazon CloudWatch: Metrics, Logs and Alarms

  • Amazon CloudWatch monitors AWS resources and applications in real time
  • Metrics track performance data, dashboards show it in one place, and alarms watch metrics against thresholds
  • Alarms can notify you and trigger automated actions
  • CloudWatch Logs collects, stores and queries logs
  • Many AWS services send basic metrics for free
Exam tip

Is it healthy right now, and who should be told if not? CloudWatch.

AWS Config: What Changed, and Is It Compliant?

  • AWS Config gives a detailed view of resource configuration, how resources relate, and how they changed over time
  • Config rules check settings and flag noncompliant resources; conformance packs bundle rules
  • Aggregators give one view across accounts and Regions
  • Useful for auditing, security analysis and finding the last known good configuration
Exam tip

What changed, and does it meet our rules? AWS Config.

CloudTrail, CloudWatch or Config?

The question Service
Which user called which API, and when? AWS CloudTrail
Is CPU high right now? Alert me Amazon CloudWatch
How was this security group set last month? AWS Config
Does this resource break our rules? AWS Config
Keep a record of account activity for auditors AWS CloudTrail
Exam tip

Activity is CloudTrail, health is CloudWatch, configuration is Config.

AWS Control Tower: Governing Many Accounts

  • AWS Control Tower sets up and governs a multi-account environment following best practices
  • It builds a landing zone, orchestrating AWS Organizations, Service Catalog and IAM Identity Center
  • Controls (guardrails) are high-level rules: preventive, detective or proactive
  • Account Factory provisions new accounts from approved templates
  • A dashboard shows accounts, controls and noncompliant resources

Exam tip

Set up and govern many accounts the same way: AWS Control Tower.

Access Reports and Security Services Old name

  • The IAM credential report lists users and the state of their passwords, access keys and MFA (multi-factor authentication) devices, as a CSV (comma-separated values) file, up to every four hours
  • Amazon GuardDuty detects threats from sources such as CloudTrail events, VPC flow logs and DNS (Domain Name System) logs
  • Amazon Inspector scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities
  • AWS Security Hub collects findings and checks standards; the docs now call it Security Hub CSPM
  • AWS Shield Standard protects against DDoS (distributed denial of service) attacks at no extra charge (Module 5)
Exam tip

Detect threats: GuardDuty. Scan for vulnerabilities: Inspector. One view of findings: Security Hub.

What the Exam Asks: Responsibility and Governance

  • Of the cloud or in the cloud: AWS's infrastructure, or your configuration and data
  • Inherited, shared or customer-specific: all from AWS, both sides, or yours alone
  • CloudTrail, CloudWatch or Config: who did it, how healthy, or what changed
  • KMS or ACM: keys for data, or certificates for websites
  • Artifact or Config: AWS's reports, or your own resource history
  • EC2, RDS or Lambda: how much AWS manages for you
Exam tip

Name the situation first, then the model or service.

Design Check: Tidewater's Security Plan

Tidewater's need Choose
Understand who secures what Shared responsibility: AWS of the cloud, Tidewater in the cloud
Prove AWS's compliance to the auditor AWS Artifact reports
Find who deleted a security group AWS CloudTrail
Alert on high CPU on the web servers Amazon CloudWatch alarm
Check settings against its rules AWS Config rules
Encrypt customer data at rest AWS KMS keys
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for the physical security of AWS data centers?

  • AThe customer who stores data in the facility
  • BAWS, as part of security of the cloud
  • CThe customer's chosen colocation partner
  • DEach Region's local government office
Show the answer

Answer: B. Physical security of the facilities is part of security of the cloud, which AWS owns. Customers inherit these controls and do not manage the data centers themselves.

S2Which task is the customer's responsibility for an Amazon EC2 instance?

  • AReplacing failed server hardware in the data center
  • BMaintaining the hypervisor that runs the instances
  • CProviding power and cooling for the facility
  • DApplying security patches to the guest operating system
Show the answer

Answer: D. On EC2 the customer manages the guest operating system, including its updates and patches. AWS handles the hardware, the virtualization layer and the facility.

S3Tidewater runs its database on Amazon RDS. Which TWO tasks does AWS handle? (Select TWO.)

  • APatching the database engine software
  • BTuning the shop's slow SQL queries
  • CPatching the operating system of the database host
  • DDeciding who may connect through IAM and security groups
  • EChoosing which customer data to store in the database
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. With Amazon RDS, AWS patches the database software and the operating system. Query tuning, access control and the choice of data remain the customer's responsibility.

S4Tidewater moves a function to AWS Lambda. Which task stays with Tidewater?

  • AWriting and securing the function code and its permissions
  • BPatching the servers that run the function
  • CProvisioning capacity for sudden bursts of traffic
  • DMaintaining the operating system of the runtime
Show the answer

Answer: A. Lambda manages servers, capacity, scaling and patching. The customer provides the code and the permissions it needs, and remains responsible for the data it handles.

S5Which term describes controls that a customer fully inherits from AWS, such as physical and environmental controls?

  • ACustomer-specific controls
  • BShared controls
  • CInherited controls
  • DCompensating controls
Show the answer

Answer: C. Inherited controls come entirely from AWS. Shared controls apply to both sides, and customer-specific controls are solely the customer's, based on its application.

S6Which is an example of a shared control?

  • APhysical access to the data centers
  • BPatch management
  • CRouting data within a customer's own security zones
  • DThe hardware lifecycle of the host servers
Show the answer

Answer: B. Patch management is shared: AWS patches its infrastructure and the customer patches what it runs. Physical access and hardware lifecycle are AWS's, and security zone routing is customer-specific.

S7Tidewater stores customer photos in Amazon S3. Which responsibility belongs to Tidewater?

  • AOperating and maintaining the infrastructure that provides S3 storage
  • BPatching the operating systems of the servers behind S3
  • CChoosing who may access the photos and which encryption options to use
  • DReplacing failed storage hardware in the data centers
Show the answer

Answer: C. On an abstracted service such as S3, AWS runs the infrastructure and platform, while the customer manages its data, encryption options and access permissions.

S8Which TWO describe AWS Artifact? (Select TWO.)

  • AIt provides on-demand downloads of AWS compliance reports
  • BIt records every API call made in an account
  • CIt lets you review and accept agreements with AWS
  • DIt detects threats by analyzing network logs
  • EIt creates the keys used to encrypt data
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. AWS Artifact offers compliance reports and agreements. CloudTrail records API calls, GuardDuty detects threats and AWS KMS manages encryption keys.

S9Tidewater's auditor asks for AWS's SOC report. Where can Tidewater download it?

  • AAWS Artifact
  • BAWS Config
  • CAmazon CloudWatch
  • DAWS Control Tower
Show the answer

Answer: A. AWS Artifact provides on-demand downloads of AWS compliance reports such as SOC, ISO and PCI. Config, CloudWatch and Control Tower do not provide AWS's own audit reports.

S10Tidewater needs to learn which user deleted a security group yesterday. Which service records this?

  • AAmazon CloudWatch alarms
  • BAWS Config rules
  • CAWS CloudTrail
  • DAWS Key Management Service
Show the answer

Answer: C. CloudTrail records account activity, showing who took which action and when. CloudWatch watches metrics, Config tracks configuration, and AWS KMS manages encryption keys.

S11Which service records how a resource was configured in the past and flags settings that break your rules?

  • AAWS CloudTrail
  • BAWS Config
  • CAmazon CloudWatch Logs
  • DAWS Artifact
Show the answer

Answer: B. AWS Config keeps resource configuration history and evaluates it against rules. CloudTrail records activity, CloudWatch Logs stores log data, and Artifact provides compliance documents.

S12Which statement about AWS KMS is correct?

  • AIt issues SSL/TLS certificates for websites and renews them automatically
  • BIt records the API activity of every user in the account
  • CIt routes network traffic between virtual private clouds
  • DIt creates and controls the keys used to encrypt and sign data
Show the answer

Answer: D. AWS KMS creates and controls encryption and signing keys. Certificates are managed by AWS Certificate Manager, API activity by CloudTrail and routing by networking services.

S13Tidewater wants customer data protected in transit and at rest. Which TWO actions fit? (Select TWO.)

  • AUse TLS for connections between customers and the shop
  • BTurn off all logging to reduce the amount of stored data
  • CEncrypt stored data with keys managed in AWS KMS
  • DShare the root user password with the auditors
  • EKeep card numbers in plain text so lookups stay fast
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. TLS protects data in transit, and encryption with KMS keys protects data at rest. Turning off logging, sharing the root password and storing plain text all weaken security.

S14Tidewater is adding many AWS accounts and wants standard account setup with guardrails. Which service helps?

  • AAWS Control Tower
  • BAWS Artifact
  • CAmazon Inspector
  • DAWS Certificate Manager
Show the answer

Answer: A. AWS Control Tower sets up and governs a multi-account environment with controls and Account Factory. Artifact provides reports, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities and ACM manages certificates.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Shared responsibility AWS secures the cloud; you secure what you put in it; responsibility shifts with the service
Controls inherited from AWS, shared (patching, configuration, training), or customer-specific
Services EC2 is mostly yours, RDS has AWS manage the platform, Lambda has AWS manage the servers
Compliance AWS Artifact for AWS's reports and agreements; compliance varies by location, industry and service
Encryption TLS in transit, server-side or client-side at rest; KMS for keys, ACM for certificates
Governance CloudTrail for activity, CloudWatch for health, Config for configuration, Control Tower for many accounts
